chunks: He was asked about a man who sleeps, then wakes up and touches his private part and sees some wetness, while he did not see anything in his dream: should he perform ghusl (ritual bath)?
He said: 'No. Ghusl is only from the greater fluid.'

key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْأَكْبَرِ: the major fluid, meaning semen in this context
key_terms.بَلَلًا: wetness or moisture found on the body or garment
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: to perform ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required if a person wakes up and finds wetness without seeing anything in a dream?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity after sleep. It states that merely finding wetness without evidence of major discharge does not make ghusl obligatory; ghusl is required only upon the emission of the major fluid.
